title: Incident detection performance and acceptance criteria
test_type: Document review and controlled performance test
assurance_question: Are detection capabilities evaluated against approved, use-specific performance criteria across relevant operating conditions?
objective: Establish whether detection performance, false positives and false negatives can be evaluated against defined acceptance thresholds.
proposed_procedure: Review the defined detection categories, model or analytics configuration, test plan, dataset selection and ground-truth method. If authorised access and a suitable test environment become available, test representative cases across relevant conditions and report results by detection category and condition.
required_evidence: Approved detection requirements and thresholds; model/configuration documentation; test plan and test cases; representative labelled data or controlled scenarios; results by category and operating condition; finding-remediation records.
pass_criteria: Detection categories and acceptance thresholds are defined before testing; the test method and data are appropriate to intended use; results are reproducible and reported against each threshold; critical and high-severity test findings are resolved before the relevant validation milestone.
exception_criteria: Acceptance thresholds are absent or unsuitable; datasets or scenarios do not represent intended conditions; results fail approved criteria; false positives or false negatives are not measured; or critical/high findings remain unresolved at the validation milestone.
prerequisites: Documented intended use and detection categories; approved thresholds; authorised access to configuration and test evidence; and, for technical testing, an approved test environment and suitable labelled data.
limitations: This entry defines an assurance activity only. No live-system test, configuration review or performance evaluation has been performed as part of this portfolio.

title: Authorisation, human review and override of automated protocols
assurance_question: Who can authorise, review, stop or override a protocol or alert, and what happens when the trigger or information is incorrect?
objective: Establish whether the intended operational workflow provides clear authority, human review where required, escalation, override and fallback arrangements.
proposed_procedure: Review workflow diagrams, operating procedures, role assignments and relevant permissions. Walk through scenarios involving a false detection, conflicting information, an urgent priority incident, a communications failure and an attempted cancellation or override. If access is authorised, inspect supporting configuration, logs and test evidence.
required_evidence: Protocol trigger rules; role and responsibility matrix; approval and escalation procedures; override/cancellation and fallback instructions; access configuration; operator training evidence; relevant audit logs and test results.
pass_criteria: Trigger conditions and responsible roles are clear; required approvals and human review points are documented; operators can exercise the specified override or cancellation powers; degraded/failure scenarios have defined handling; and the workflow can be evidenced through appropriate test records or logs.
exception_criteria: Authority is ambiguous; consequential actions lack required review; override or fallback arrangements are absent or ineffective; failure scenarios are not addressed; or records are insufficient to reconstruct relevant decisions.
prerequisites: Current workflow and role documentation; participation by appropriate operational and technical representatives for a walkthrough; authorised access to configurations or logs if these are examined.
limitations: A documented procedure alone does not establish effective operation. Any walkthrough or technical verification must be performed and recorded before the test can be marked as executed.

title: Predictive-model purpose, validation and uncertainty handling
assurance_question: Are the prediction targets, evaluation metrics, acceptance thresholds and limitations defined and supported by appropriate validation evidence?
objective: Determine whether the predictive function is adequately specified and validated for its intended public-safety use, and whether limitations and uncertainty are communicated appropriately.
proposed_procedure: First identify the specific prediction target and intended decision use. Review the model development/evaluation documentation, data selection, approved metrics and thresholds, assumptions affecting continued validity, and maintenance/retraining plans. If authorised model access and suitable data become available, assess performance on appropriate evaluation data, including temporal or geographic variation where relevant, and compare results with the approved criteria.
required_evidence: Model purpose and target definitions; CRISP-DM documentation where applicable; data description and provenance; evaluation methodology and results; RMC approval of proposed metrics and thresholds; calibration or uncertainty documentation where relevant; monitoring and maintenance/retraining records.
pass_criteria: Prediction targets and intended use are explicit; metrics and acceptable thresholds are approved by the RMC as required by the specification; evaluation data and methods are appropriate to the use; results are assessed against thresholds; limitations and uncertainty are documented; and required remediation or revalidation is evidenced.
exception_criteria: Targets or permitted use remain ambiguous; metrics or thresholds are absent or unapproved; evaluation data are unsuitable; results fail approved thresholds; material limitations are concealed; or maintenance and revalidation needs are not addressed.
prerequisites: Access to the model and its documentation; a defined prediction target and intended use; suitable evaluation data; approved metrics and thresholds; and authorisation for any technical testing.
limitations: The reviewed specification does not establish the actual prediction targets or validation results. Technical testing cannot be completed without suitable authorised access and evidence. This test has not been executed.

title: Event-correlation logic, provenance and error handling
test_type: Document review and controlled scenario test
assurance_question: Does event correlation correctly link related reports, preserve source provenance, and handle duplicate, conflicting, incomplete or delayed information?
objective: Determine whether the event-correlation behaviour is specified, testable and supported by evidence appropriate to its intended operational use.
proposed_procedure: Review event definitions, correlation rules/model documentation, source mappings, data-quality assumptions, and test plans/results. If authorised test access is available, run controlled scenarios representing same-event reports, unrelated reports, duplicates, conflicting attributes, incomplete records and delayed inputs; compare outcomes with pre-defined expected results.
required_evidence: Event definitions and matching criteria; source/interface mappings; data dictionary and lineage; approved test cases and expected results; labelled or controlled test inputs; correlation outputs and error logs; remediation records.
pass_criteria: Expected behaviour is defined for each scenario; source provenance is retained; false links and missed links are measured against pre-defined criteria; conflicting, incomplete and delayed data have documented handling; results and exceptions are reproducible and traceable.
exception_criteria: Matching criteria or expected results are undefined; provenance cannot be traced; material scenarios are not tested; results fail approved criteria; or incorrect links/missed links lack defined correction and escalation.
prerequisites: Access to design and test documentation; defined event types and expected outcomes; authorised test environment and suitable test data for technical execution.
limitations: No correlation test has been executed. The procedure is proposed and depends on access to design artefacts and, for technical testing, an authorised environment.

title: Cross-module purposes, data fields and access safeguards
test_type: Document review and data-flow traceability review
assurance_question: What safety-related information is shared with the CRM/fidelity module, for which purposes, and under which access, retention and reuse safeguards?
objective: Establish whether the documented design limits cross-module processing to defined purposes and whether data transfers and safeguards can be traced.
proposed_procedure: Obtain and compare the Public Safety-to-CRM data-flow diagram, field mapping, purpose descriptions and relevant privacy/governance documentation. Trace each specified field to its purpose, recipient, access roles, retention/deletion rule and any campaign/personalisation use. If permitted, inspect configured interfaces, access rules and relevant records to compare actual configuration with approved documentation.
required_evidence: Cross-module data-flow/interface specification; field-level mapping and data dictionary; purpose and role descriptions; applicable privacy assessment and transparency materials; access matrix; retention/deletion schedule; campaign-use rules; configuration or audit evidence where available.
pass_criteria: Each transferred field and purpose is documented; access and retention rules are assigned; reuse for personalisation/campaigns is explicitly addressed and justified; safeguards and restrictions are reflected in design/configuration evidence; unresolved legal or governance questions are escalated rather than assumed away.
exception_criteria: Fields or purposes cannot be identified; campaign reuse is not addressed; access or retention boundaries are missing or contradictory; actual configuration conflicts with approved documentation; or claims about safeguards lack supporting evidence.
prerequisites: Availability of current cross-module design documents and governance records; participation by relevant system/data owners; authorised access to configuration or logs if implementation is reviewed.
limitations: This is a proposed documentary/configuration review, not a conclusion that data are currently transferred or unlawfully used. The specification describes a relationship but does not establish live data flows.

title: Video and drone data capture, access, export and retention controls
test_type: Document review and configuration/operational test where authorised
assurance_question: Are camera and drone capture, access, export, retention and deletion arrangements defined and implemented for the documented purposes?
objective: Determine whether video and drone data handling can be traced to documented purposes, permissions, retention settings and operating procedures.
proposed_procedure: Review camera/drone deployment and configuration records, enabled analytics, access permissions, export procedures and retention rules. Verify how the specified minimum 30-day local video storage requirement for critical channels is configured without assuming that this is the appropriate retention period for every data category. For drone operations, review deployment authorisation and footage/telemetry handling. If authorised, sample configuration and logs and test retention/deletion or access controls in a controlled environment.
required_evidence: Camera and drone inventory/configuration; deployment locations and enabled analytics; purpose and operating procedures; access matrix; export and access logs; retention schedule by data category; deletion/rotation evidence; commissioning records; drone deployment and telemetry handling procedures.
pass_criteria: Data capture and enabled analytics are linked to documented purposes; access and export permissions are role-based and evidenced; retention rules distinguish relevant data categories and the critical-channel minimum; deletion/rotation and logging operate as specified; drone deployment and telemetry handling responsibilities are documented.
exception_criteria: Enabled features or deployment locations are unknown; access/export is not appropriately restricted or evidenced; retention rules are missing or conflated across data categories; deletion cannot be verified; or drone capture/handling lacks documented procedures.
prerequisites: Access to current camera/drone configuration, retention and access records; authorised operators/system administrators for walkthroughs; approval and safe test environment for any configuration or deletion test.
limitations: No system configuration or operational test has been performed. The procurement requirements alone do not prove deployment, configuration or safeguard effectiveness.

title: Security controls and connected-system integration
test_type: Document review and authorised security/integration testing
assurance_question: Are connected-system interfaces appropriately protected, and can security-relevant events be detected, investigated and traced?
objective: Assess whether the documented interface, access-control, logging and integration requirements are supported by implementation and test evidence.
proposed_procedure: Review interface specifications, authentication and authorisation arrangements, API security requirements, integration test results, centralised logging configuration and relevant audit/monitoring procedures. If authorised testing is available, execute approved negative and failure-path tests in a controlled environment and verify logging and alert behaviour.
required_evidence: Interface and network documentation; access-control configuration; API security requirements; integration and security test cases/results; logging configuration and sample events; monitoring and remediation records.
pass_criteria: Interface permissions and security requirements are documented; integration tests cover expected and failure scenarios; relevant actions and security events are logged and traceable; material findings are resolved or formally handled before the relevant acceptance milestone.
exception_criteria: Interfaces or permissions are insufficiently documented; required failure scenarios are not tested; relevant security events cannot be traced; tests fail acceptance criteria; or material findings remain unresolved without an approved disposition.
prerequisites: Current interface and security documentation; relevant technical owners; authorised access to configuration and logs; written approval and a controlled environment for any technical tests.
limitations: No security assessment or integration test has been executed for this portfolio. The test requires authorised evidence and, for technical testing, an approved environment.

title: Backup, recording and service-recovery readiness
test_type: Document review and controlled restoration test
assurance_question: Can required video and operational information be recovered within approved objectives after a relevant failure, and can the recovery process be evidenced?
objective: Establish whether the specified resilience, backup, recording and restoration requirements are implemented and tested.
proposed_procedure: Review the resilience design, backup scope and schedules, recording redundancy, retention requirements, restoration procedures, recovery objectives and test results. If authorised, observe or execute a controlled restoration test and compare the recovered data and elapsed recovery time with pre-approved criteria.
required_evidence: As-built resilience design; backup configuration and logs; recording redundancy evidence; data-category retention mapping; documented recovery objectives; restoration test plan/results; failure and escalation records.
pass_criteria: Backup and recording coverage is defined; restoration procedures and recovery objectives are approved; test results demonstrate recovery of required data within the approved criteria; failures and exceptions are recorded and addressed.
exception_criteria: Required information is not covered by backups; recovery objectives are absent; restoration cannot be demonstrated; results fail approved criteria; or failures are not recorded and remediated.
prerequisites: Access to current backup/recovery documentation and responsible technical staff; approved recovery objectives and test cases; authorised test environment and safeguards against disruption or data loss.
limitations: No restoration or resilience test has been performed. Procurement requirements alone do not demonstrate successful recovery.

title: Ongoing AI performance monitoring and degradation detection
assurance_question: Are model-specific performance baselines, approved thresholds and ongoing monitoring arrangements defined, reviewed and acted on?
objective: Determine whether deterioration in detection, correlation or predictive performance can be identified and addressed during operation.
proposed_procedure: Identify each function's approved performance measures and thresholds. Review baseline and ongoing evaluation results, monitoring frequency, input/data drift indicators, alert and review responsibilities, maintenance/retraining records, and examples of corrective action. If authorised operational evidence is available, trace a sample of monitoring alerts through review and disposition.
required_evidence: Model-specific metrics and thresholds; approval records; baseline and ongoing evaluation reports; monitoring dashboards or logs; drift assessments; review records; maintenance/retraining and corrective-action evidence.
pass_criteria: Relevant metrics and thresholds are defined and appropriately approved; monitoring evidence covers the intended functions and relevant conditions; exceptions trigger documented review; and required corrective action or revalidation can be traced to closure.
exception_criteria: Thresholds or baselines are missing; monitoring does not cover relevant functions or conditions; significant exceptions are not investigated; or changes and corrective actions lack adequate evidence.
prerequisites: Defined AI functions and intended uses; approved performance measures; access to monitoring and lifecycle records; authorised operational representatives if walkthroughs are required.
limitations: This is a proposed review. The existence of KPI or model-lifecycle requirements does not prove that function-specific monitoring operates effectively.

title: AI-related incident investigation and material-change control
assurance_question: Are AI-related failures and material changes reported, assessed, approved, tested, tracked and resolved through accountable processes?
objective: Determine whether incidents and changes affecting AI-enabled functions have defined ownership, escalation, impact assessment, verification and closure procedures.
proposed_procedure: Review incident and change-management procedures, role assignments, severity criteria, approval and rollback rules, and post-incident review requirements. If records are available and access is authorised, trace a sample of relevant incidents or changes from identification through assessment, approval, testing, implementation, monitoring and closure.
required_evidence: Incident taxonomy and workflow; accountable role map; incident and change records; impact assessments; approval history; test evidence; rollback/fallback procedures; post-incident reviews; corrective-action tracking.
pass_criteria: Responsibilities and escalation routes are defined; material changes receive documented impact assessment and appropriate approval/testing; incidents are investigated and corrective actions tracked; relevant decisions and outcomes are auditable.
exception_criteria: Ownership or escalation is unclear; material changes bypass required assessment or approval; incidents are not tracked to resolution; rollback/fallback arrangements are undefined where needed; or records do not support reconstruction of decisions.
prerequisites: Current incident and change procedures; access to relevant records; participation by responsible governance and technical roles for a walkthrough.
limitations: No operational incident or change-management process has been inspected or tested for this portfolio.

title: External indicator integration, provenance and data-quality validation
test_type: Conditional document review and data-lineage assessment
assurance_question: Do any Annex I external sources feed Public Safety Module #32, and, if so, are their provenance, freshness, suitability and quality controls defined?
objective: Establish whether an integration exists before assessing its data-quality controls or influence on Public Safety outputs.
proposed_procedure: First obtain authoritative interface mappings and determine whether Annex I sources are connected to Module #32. If no connection is evidenced, record the dependency as unverified and do not infer that the risk pathway is active. If a connection is confirmed, trace selected data fields from source to use, inspect source ownership and refresh frequency, review validation and transformation rules, and assess monitoring and error handling.
required_evidence: Module #32 interface mappings; data lineage and data dictionary; source owner and provenance records; data refresh/freshness rules; transformations and validation logic; data-quality monitoring results; documented use of indicators in analysis or prediction.
pass_criteria: The existence or absence of the interface is evidenced; any connected source has documented ownership, provenance, fields, transformations, freshness and suitability criteria; quality exceptions are monitored and handled; and the influence of data on relevant outputs is traceable.
exception_criteria: The interface cannot be established; a confirmed source lacks provenance or appropriate quality checks; stale or invalid data are accepted without defined handling; or material data-quality exceptions cannot be traced and resolved.
prerequisites: Authoritative interface documentation; access to source and integration specifications; data owners or technical representatives if a connection is confirmed; authorised sample data for any detailed technical assessment.
limitations: The specification lists Annex I sources for PIDM but does not establish their connection to Module #32. Any assessment of Public Safety use must remain conditional until an interface is evidenced.
